narrative_events.details: Śaunaka asks location and manifestation date. Sūta places Vakratunda at the eastern limit, installed by gods/sages/Gaṇas, manifest on Bhādra bright fourth; midday worship gives immense siddhis, beginning/end less. Images lie in each island/region’s east; square field ten yojanas, deity central with Siddhi left/Buddhi right, lion in front, eight siddhis in eight directions, eight Gaṇas and Śiva/Viṣṇu/Sun/Śakti in four directions.

Brahmā and deities occupy east/behind, Gaṅgā and rivers south, Kāśī and fields west, Vasiṣṭha and sages north. Śeṣa/Nāga kings, Gandharvas, mountains, Siddhas, Apsarases, Vidyādharas and Kinnaras serve joyfully and exchange Vakratunda stories; bathing in the ocean they create tīrthas bearing their names.

Gaṇeśa tīrtha bathing fulfils life; pilgrimage gives desired ends; dying in the field gives Brahman state. Distant remembrance gives enduring liberation by śukla-gati; devotees anywhere attain Brahman and purify people by sight. Sūta limits his account: even Śeṣa, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Vedas, Skanda and yogins cannot exhaust it, and he repeats Mudgala’s account to Dakṣa.

Śaunaka asks what followed Mudgala’s discourse to Dakṣa. Dakṣa asks the detailed Dhundhirāja incarnation and how Vakratunda is born from Śaṅkara’s body. Mudgala introduces an old Gaṇeśa account Yājñavalkya taught Kauśika, illuminating Brahminhood.

Bhārgava sage Ṛcīka grows old through long austerity, sees deer with mates/descendants, desires household life and asks king Gādhi’s daughter. Gādhi demands a thousand dark-eared horses as his established marriage-price. Ṛcīka gets them from Varuṇa and gives them; frightened Gādhi duly marries his daughter to him. Her mother laments, provides goods/clothes and sends her to the forest, where she diligently serves Ṛcīka.

Pleased by his wife’s good conduct, Ṛcīka uses his own austerity to create a richly adorned forest city with four social classes, servants and wealth, and adopts a youthful form. He enjoys marriage properly, then judges its pleasures small and becomes unattached.

The queen visits with wealth/clothes and finds a magnificent city rather than the hermitage; a sweeper identifies Ṛcīka’s city and summons her daughter. Seeing the prosperous sage, she tells her daughter to ask him for sons for both women. Ṛcīka prepares two carus/puroḍāśas with Brahmin/Kṣatriya potency and specifies each eater, then leaves for midday rites. The mother orders exchanging their portions; daughter complies, mother returns home, both become pregnant.

Ṛcīka sees fierce radiance in his wife and asks about Kṣatriya potency. She admits the exchange; he predicts her brother will be an ascetic, her son a fierce bowman. Afraid, she asks a Brahmin son and threatens her life otherwise. He shifts that quality to her grandson, informs Viṣṇu of the pregnancy and effects it through tapas. Jamadagni is born to him; Rāma, best bearer of weapons, becomes Jamadagni’s son. Gādhi’s queen bears Viśvāmitra in ninth month; Gādhi installs his grown son in the kingdom and leaves for austerity.

King Viśvāmitra hunts, grows hungry/thirsty and reaches Vasiṣṭha’s hermitage. Vasiṣṭha feeds king and army by the cow’s power. Viśvāmitra requests Nandinī; refused, he orders her seizure. She destroys the messengers; when men whip her, she creates a great army which destroys the king’s whole army. He returns defeated.

Viśvāmitra leaves rule to ministers and propitiates Śaṅkara in forest. At100 years Śiva grants complete missile knowledge. He returns, attacks Vasiṣṭha and hermitage with fire missile and other weapons. Vasiṣṭha’s Brahmadaṇḍa destroys every missile and defeats him; he flees. Brahmins comfort Vasiṣṭha. Viśvāmitra recognizes Brahmin power’s superiority and his destroyed weapons.

Viśvāmitra abandons kingdom, fasts and repeats Gāyatrī by puraścaraṇa for Brahminhood, scorching the world. At10,000 years Brahmā offers a boon; his Brahminhood request is answered with further austerity. Brahmā comes ten times offering another boon, which he refuses. His tapas subjects gods and awes Brahmins into assent to his claimed Brahmarṣi rank; Vasiṣṭha still calls him Rājarṣi. Furious, he repeatedly attempts Vasiṣṭha’s death without success and remains distressed.

Yājñavalkya, explicitly arisen from Brahmā’s limb, visits. Viśvāmitra bows, worships and says birth, study and austerity bear fruit through seeing him; he asks the visit’s purpose and offers obedience as his servant.

Yājñavalkya came only because he knew Viśvāmitra’s grief, promises to remove it by reasoned knowledge, and hears the denied boon and Vasiṣṭha’s Rājarṣi address. He promises Brahmarṣi rank after relinquishing pride/envy and offers the Kāśī–Viśveśvara story: their inseparability even at dissolution produces pride and a separating obstacle. Viśvāmitra asks its nature.

After60 rainless years and terrestrial devastation, Brahmā approaches Sūrya-line king Divodāsa, who left rule and performs devotional tapas for liberation. Brahmā asks him to take Kāśī to save life, promising rainfall if he rules. He first refuses, asking liberation; then compassionately accepts on condition earthly rule excludes gods, while gods/heaven, humans/earth and Nāgas/Rākṣasas/Pātāla keep their domains. He will worship Śambhu as a deity; Brahmā agrees and grants Kāśī.

Brahmā takes Śiva with gods/sages to Mandara to grant Marīci a boon, warning the ascetic will die otherwise. Marīci asks liberation; suffering from tapas he relinquishes life, obtains Śiva’s likeness and reaches Kailāsa. Brahmā then asks Śiva to remain at Mandara, explaining Divodāsa’s condition for drought relief and asking pardon. Śiva agrees with a sigh and stays with Pārvatī/Gaṇas.

Śiva laments that Avimukta was taken from him and his Viśvanātha title is powerless. Recognizing obstacle and removal of pride, he resolves refuge in Vighnarāja and meditates on Gaṇeśa at the mountain for Kāśī. Personified Kāśī hears his departure, loses pride and meditates on Vighneśa for Śiva. Divodāsa’s righteous reign restores rain, joy and sinless observance of social duties.

Healthy people, fruitful trees, abundant cow milk, sacrifices and svāhā/svadhā please gods/ancestors. Divodāsa’s daily circuit worships Dhundhi first, then Viśveśvara, Jagadambā, Kāśī, Maṇikarṇī, Bhāgīrathī, Mādhava, Jaigīṣavya cave, Kālabhairava and Daṇḍapāṇi. He makes people perform this and punishes the unrighteous;80,000 years pass without even slight sin entering.

Gods resent loss of earthly sovereignty and scheme against the king. Indra orders Agni to withdraw outward fire; people seek Divodāsa, who assumes fire-form by tapas everywhere on earth. As other gods withdraw he supplies their functions through forms including Vāyu, unknown to the people. Gods ask Brahmā what to do; he sends them to request restored places. They praise Divodāsa, he praises them and restores their offices, remaining in one human body. Agni and others resume their places. The transcription misnumbers sequential63 as33.

Śiva grieves that the righteous tapas-powered king cannot be displaced. Gods/sages offer to lure citizens by siddhis so their sin falls on king, then Śiva can take Kāśī. Their many forms and siddhis fail for a year because citizens remain righteous. Śiva’s further dispatched Bhairavas, Ādityas, Vasus, sages, Yoginīs and Gaṇas fail. Brahmā is sent and performs ten Aśvamedhas, then becomes quiet.

Śiva meditates on Vighnarāja for one year, asking freedom from obstacles and separation. Seeing complete humility, Vakratunda manifests lion-mounted, four-armed, noose/goad/boon/fearlessness, red elephant face, great belly, Siddhi/Buddhi, Śeṣa at navel and Cintāmaṇi. Śiva worships/hymns creator/preserver/destroyer and causal/transcendent forms, seeks inseparable Kāśī, and recalls an earlier promise to appear in son-relation on remembrance. Vakratunda promises hymn recitation/hearing gives siddhis, enjoyment/liberation and all other requests, restoring Avimukta meaning.

Vakratunda creates a beautiful all-knowing radiant Brahmin from his body and directs him to delude Kāśī citizens and Divodāsa and restore rule to Śiva. People will call him Dhundhi the astrologer and honor him, his descendants likewise. The Brahmin bows, circles and goes remembering Gaṇeśa. Vakratunda commands Viṣṇu to enter Kāśī in Buddhist form and corrupt the already-deluded city. Viṣṇu obeys; both accomplish the ordered delusion and corruption.

Kāśī meditates for a thousand years; lion-mounted adorned Gaṇeśa arrives. She rises, bows, worships and hymns infinite/formless/formful, Siddhi/Buddhi lord, protector and obstacle-giver to nondevotees. Afflicted separation makes her Avimukta name empty; she asks Śiva’s sight. He promises return, meaningful Avimukta name, hymn that removes separation, desired ends and Brahman state to faithful reciters/hearers. He disappears; she keeps meditating, awaiting the time.

Dhundhi astrologer instantly deludes the city; Viṣṇu as Buddha then corrupts it. Divodāsa is instructed by Dhundhi and gives up rule through the Buddhist figure, awaiting Śiva. Both summon Śiva, who leads worshipped Gaṇeśa into Kāśī as first resident, then enters with gods/sages. Kāśī bows to both; gods/sages take places and Śiva grants Divodāsa liberation.

Gaṇeśa tells Śiva he restored Kāśī and will return to his own abode, visible again on Śiva’s remembrance; he disappears with Dhundhi Brahmin. Śiva creates and installs his image with gods/Brahmins, worships and announces: worship Dhundhi before pleasing Śiva to receive enjoyment/liberation, otherwise not; Vakratunda gives Kāśī-residence fruit. Naming the discovered Vedic root Dhundhirāja, Śiva credits him with four human aims and devotes daily service.

Yājñavalkya applies the example: worship Vighnarāja and abandon pride to become Brahmin. Viśvāmitra asks where pride resides, how to abandon it and how to worship/understand Gaṇeśa. The teacher identifies certainty that one’s own tapas must confer Brahminhood as pride. Practise sincerely but accept the deity’s grant or continued Rājarṣi status, knowing embodied dependence. Abandon competitiveness, think oneself below all Brahmins/ascetics and inwardly honor them. He reproaches Viśvāmitra’s envy: destruction of Vasiṣṭha’s100 sons as by a Rākṣasa, alternate creation for Triśaṅku and attempts on Vasiṣṭha’s life. Without reform even a thousand yugas of tapas ends in death.

Yājñavalkya recounts former Vakratunda deeds. Viśvāmitra, astonished, requests experiential teaching. Yājñavalkya promises his own past knowledge-giving story: visiting Vaikuṇṭha, he honored Nārāyaṇa and asked the essence and support of all beings, despite his intuition that all rests on Nārāyaṇa.

Nārāyaṇa says the world rests on Gaṇeśa: he gives inner buddhi and outer siddhi, is worshipped first, abides at beginning/middle/end, is Brahman-form lord of Siddhi/Buddhi while the others are guṇa-form. His Svānanda realm transcends oppositions and is inaccessible to sages/gods. Knowing him releases bonds.

Envious principles dispute who is highest and claim to create/preserve/destroy the supported world freely. Guṇādhīśa comes in Brahmin guise to end dispute and give knowledge. They wonder how he entered their Brahman paths; he says yoga made the path and asks the quarrel. Asked which principle is greatest, he proposes each leave the world in turn; the one whose departure breaks it is lord.

Earth withdraws, then water, tejas, wind, space and tanmātras, without destroying world. Five elements/tanmātras stand powerless and grieve. Five knowledge-senses, action-senses, Indra-form Brahman and illuminating deity-hosts next leave; the world remains as before and the withdrawn principles/deities lose radiance.

Anna-Brahman, prāṇa-form, mind-form, vijñāna, ānanda, nāda, bindu, so’ham, bodha, videha, asat, sat, sama-svavedya and neti-svavedya successively withdraw and world remains. Finally Svānanda-form withdraws and world dissolves.

Astonished principles praise Svānanda and ask him, their common support, to become Vināyaka, leader of all principles, and recreate the world as before. Vināyaka recreates it; Brahman-form principles reenter their own places and rejoice. Nārāyaṇa explains their Jagadīśvara titles in this framework.

Nārāyaṇa distinguishes Vināyaka as Nijānanda in saṃyoga and Nirānanda in ayoga, and yoga-form when that duality is dissolved, lord of Brahmans. Knowing him gives peace, so he urges worship. Vakratunda destroys the crooked deluding māyā by his trunk through devotion. Ga denotes mind/speech world, ṇa what exceeds it, and Gaṇeśa their lord/yoga-form; attaining him gives Brahman state. The Vedānta secret should be guarded for siddhi. Nārāyaṇa ceases, repeatedly saluting Gaṇeśa.

Yājñavalkya says he bowed to Janārdana, returned to forest, progressively mastered fivefold mental activity and attained Gaṇeśa by peace-yoga and grace. He urges Viśvāmitra’s refuge, offering Gāyatrī japa merit to Gaṇeśa and friendship to all so his name becomes meaningful. He departs honored, repeating Gaṇeśa’s name-mantra. Viśvāmitra thereafter abandons pride/envy, repeats Gāyatrī as offering to Gaṇeśa and meditates on him in tapas. Gāyatrī is called Veda-mother, Praṇava father, and Gaṇanātha’s Oṃ-shaped head/saguṇa identity explains the offering.

Soon Brahmā comes and grants Viśvāmitra Brahminhood. Vasiṣṭha with Brahmins honors and declares him Brahmin; sages rank him among seven Ṛṣis and chief Gaṇeśa devotees. He worships regularly and hymns Gaṇeśa.

Viśvāmitra hymns Gaṇeśa as guṇa lord/transcendent, knowledge-lord, elephant form, Brahman lord, first-worshipped, siddhi giver, māyā wielder/deluder, Buddhi lord, lion-mounted and also mouse-vehicle/bannered Heramba. Gaṇeśa appears lion-mounted with immeasurable solar brilliance; devotee falls tearful. He promises hymn hearers/reciters honor, desired ends, enjoyment/liberation, and invites boons. Viśvāmitra calls lineage, birth, tapas, fame and parents blessed by sight, declines māyā-objects and requests devotion and living among Gāṇapatyas to destroy māyā-delusion. Gaṇeśa says so be it, vanishes; Viśvāmitra becomes Gāṇapatya.

Mudgala says Vakratunda’s many manifestations give devotees siddhis and destroy demons; exhaustive telling is impossible. He closes the concise account to Dakṣa with benefits to faithful hearers/tellers/readers: sons/grandsons, wealth/grain, learning/lifespan, fruit of1000 Māgha months bathing at Prayāga, lifetime prescribed Kāśī residence,100,000 iṣṭāpūrta acts and complete sacrifices, and Brahman state. Sūta reports Mudgala ceased and he has repeated the account to Śaunaka, asking what he wishes next.

Sūta prescribes guarded transmission, prohibited recipients and anger warning; qualified transmission/questioning/speaking promises family uplift and destruction of Kali sins. Exact54.49 penalty clause is preserved only as unresolved evidence.
Sūta says he has told Vakratunda’s account devotionally, feels fulfilled through the assembly’s company and Gaṇeśa remembrance; following colophon ends first khaṇḍa.

Śaunaka’s assembly, satisfied yet hungry for more, asks Ekadanta’s Brahman nature, manifestations and acts. Sūta repeats Dakṣa’s request after Vakratunda’s account calmed his sacrifice-destruction grief. Dakṣa asks origin, vehicle and nature. Mudgala introduces an old Gṛtsamada–Prahlāda dialogue; Dakṣa asks first for Brahmā’s creation so Prahlāda’s context arises naturally. Mudgala agrees.

With Gaṇeśa’s boon Brahmā resolves creation, enters Janārdana through yogamāyā, hides in him and after a year emerges from his navel-lotus, becoming son through Viṣṇu’s boon. Meditating on Heramba, his own body releases water filling ten directions; submerged and bewildered, he remembers Vakratunda for rescue. On remembrance he sees a banyan and thumb-sized sleeping Gaṇeśa on a leaf, three-eyed, four-armed, elephant-trunked, large-bellied, Śeṣa at navel, moon/crown/adornments/clothes. The child sprays Brahmā with trunk-water; delighted Brahmā begins a hymn.

Brahmā hymns leaf-sleeping Gaṇanātha/Heramba as four-armed Śeṣa-navel, elephant-faced Lambodara/Ekadanta, thumb-sized, with Siddhi/Buddhi, creation/preservation/end and māyā-delusion power, and asks rescue from creation-obstructing flood. He sees full animate/inanimate world with lords in the mouth, is carried by varied winds into the great belly, sees many cosmic eggs, and exits by a hair-pore to see the child again.

Gaṇeśa promises Brahmā’s hymn grants all aims, enjoyment/liberation and whichever thought desired to honored reciters/hearers. He diagnoses forgotten initial remembrance/worship after navel emergence as cause of obstacle, removed now by remembrance/sight. Begin every future act with remembrance/bowing and reproduce the world seen in his belly. Child disappears; Brahmā returns to lotus, performs mantra/worship and meditation; Gaṇeśa appears in heart, receives mental worship and Siddhi/Buddhi as dakṣiṇā when they arrive there, then disappears. Brahmā bows and resolves creation.

Remembering Gaṇeśa, Brahmā emits Avidyā from body, divided fivefold, red/black/white and deluding the threefold world. Tamas obscures through ignorance/body-interest; Moha produces desires/varied enjoyment-actions; Mahāmoha wrong action/sin for bodily pleasure; Tāmisra produces sickness/poverty and mental/physical affliction; Andhatāmisra produces karmic hell-torments. Avidyā remembers Gaṇeśa and pursues her purpose; Brahmā condemns her and resolves further creation.

Four sons arise from Brahmā’s body: Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana and Sanatkumāra. Vidyā/jñāna is their mother-form, formless bodha/self nature. Their paths: Sanaka sahaja, Sanandana sama-yoga, Sanātana jñāna-yoga, Sanatkumāra karma-yoga. At Brahmā’s order to create remembering Gaṇeśa they create many yoga paths; displeased Brahmā tells them to stop yoga-creation and they comply.

Angry at knowledge-creation, Brahmā emits Śambhu as forehead-born son: five faces, three eyes, ten arms, half-female/male, crescent, trident, matted hair and tiger/elephant skins. Crying child asks father for place, names and task. Brahmā names Rudra for crying, Śiva as all-happiness ground, recalls boon giving son-form, assigns eight abodes earth/water/fire/wind/space/moon/sun/consecrated sacrificer and eleven names, and orders creation after Gaṇeśa meditation. Śiva creates countless immortal Rudras. Asked to create birth/death beings, he refuses and stays quiet, called Sthāṇu, celibate/upward-seeded and worshipping Gaṇeśa.

Brahmā emits Vedas with śāstras and Purāṇas from mouths and tells them to create. They propitiate Gaṇeśa by tapas, receive boons and create beings and varied rites. Brahmā rejoices, begins sacrifice and thinks of Viṣṇu to obtain him as son. Four-armed Yajña-form Janārdana emerges from sacrifice, asks father’s order and, remembering Gaṇeśa as told, creates many karma-born sacrifices granting manifold fruits like wish-trees.

Ten body-born sons appear: Marīci, Bhṛgu, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Dakṣa, Aṅgiras, Vasiṣṭha, Nārada. Ordered to create, they agree and go to forest tapas. Nārada refuses creation, choosing Gaṇanāyaka worship because world is māyā/mithyā; Brahmā insists create first, worship in old age. Nārada questions labour for delusive aims. Brahmā angrily curses Śūdra birth and woman-enjoying Gandharva life; Nārada curses Brahmā to be unworshipped for needless cursing.

Nārada propitiates Gaṇeśa by one-syllable mantra for100 divine years and requests curse removal after hymn. Gaṇeśa says he cannot falsify father’s curse because his prior boon makes Brahmā truthful. Instead he will teach Nārada as Gandharva so māyā cannot hurt him amid women; then Śūdra birth with renouncer company/knowledge, forest life and Vaiṣṇava path; after that body falls, he again becomes Brahmā’s son Nārada, worships Śambhu and learns Gaṇeśa from Nārāyaṇa to become a loved Gāṇapatya/yoga lord. Gaṇeśa disappears; narrator says Nārada undergoes curse, returns to heaven and is reborn as Śiva-devotee, then Nārāyaṇa teaches him Gāṇapatya devotion.

Dakṣa asks how Nārāyaṇa taught Nārada. Nārada sees Śaṅkara devotedly worshipping a jeweled Cintāmaṇi/Gaṇeśa image on Kailāsa, tearful and immersed in meditation, then approaches Viṣṇu at Vaikuṇṭha. He asks why Śiva, whom he regards as immutable unmanifest Brahman, worships another, and why Viṣṇu also chants Gaṇeśa’s name. Nārāyaṇa answers Gaṇeśa is yoga-peace, Siddhi/Buddhi lord in Svānanda, sole Vināyaka; the other deities gain siddhi-giving power by devotion and worship for yoga-peace.

Nārāyaṇa recounts asking Śiva the same question after his daily worship. Śiva explains Buddhi as fivefold mental activity/Prakṛti enjoying fivefold, Siddhi as manifold delusion for whose attainment mind strives, including four aims and Brahman state. Brahman-attainer has no fivefold mind, is yogin non-different from Gaṇeśa. Ga denotes saṃprajñāta, ṇa asaṃprajñāta; Gaṇeśa is their yoga-peace lord. Śiva names himself unmanifest/neti, Viṣṇu sama, and distinguishes bhava-pratyaya’s fivefold/māyā Gaṇeśa and upāya-pratyaya’s māyā-free, while direct Gaṇeśa transcends either and is attained by peace. He urges fivefold-mind abandonment to become Cintāmaṇi; Nārāyaṇa concludes Gaṇeśa grants their offices and Brahman state and is their family deity.

Nārada bows to Viṣṇu, practices forest yoga, mental Gaṇeśa meditation and mantra; after ten years Gaṇeśa appears. He bows and worships, hymns Veda-transcendent Brahman, beyond/within neither mind/speech category, Siddhi/Buddhi lord, remover of devotee obstacles and giver to nondevotees, delusion/yoga/Vināyaka/Cintāmaṇi/Ekadanta, moon-bearing, mouse-vehicle/bannered, creator/preserver/destroyer. He declares seeing Gaṇeśa removed differentiated death-delusion, attained peace-yoga/no difference, and requests supreme devotion and loving Gāṇapatya status.

Gaṇeśa grants permanent unwavering devotion, no departure from yoga, honor by yogins/all; Nārada’s hymn gives peace-yoga and bhukti/mukti to readers/hearers. He merges into Nārada’s heart, where the sage always sees him. Mudgala explicitly closes Nārada account and promises good destiny to its hearers/readers.
